headlines.title: San Rafael firefighters find collector 1984 DMC DeLorean engulfed in flames in garage
headlines.description: A 1984 DMC DeLorean, the car model made famous in the movie “Back to the Future,” burned Sunday afternoon after catching fire in a San Rafael garage, fire officials said. The fire was reported about 4:40 p.m. Sunday in the 100 block of Marino Drive, where the collector vehicle was destroyed along with other contents of the garage, the San Rafael Fire Department said. The rare car is known for its classic gull-wing doors, V-6 engine and stainless-steel body, which gives it a flashy silver appearance. According to DeLorean Motor Company’s buyers guide, roughly 9,000 DeLorean vehicles were created before the company shut down in 1982. Firefighters say the owner turned on the ignition and smelled “fumes and vapors,” before realizing the engine was on fire. The man tried to put out the fire with his garden hose, but because the fire was in the engine compartment he was unable to extinguish the flames before firefighters arrived. Firefighters controlled the fire in roughly 15 minutes, before it made its way into the home. The home’s two residents evacuated and weren’t injured. The cause of the fire is under investigation, but fire officials believe the blaze was started by a “mechanical malfunction” while the vehicle was running. In a press release on Monday, the fire department emphasized the importance of having an attached garage to prevent fires from spreading to a home. Firefighters recommend upkeep of “protective barriers” between the garage and living areas to help stop the spread of fire and smoke.

headlines.title: Dangerous conditions persist at Bay Area beaches
headlines.description: Bay Area beachgoers should keep an extra close eye on the water to start the week due to hazardous conditions, officials warned. A Beach Hazards Statement remains in effect through Wednesday afternoon, according to the National Weather Service. The weather service said tropical cyclones in the Eastern Pacific Ocean are stirring up a long-period swell, sending breaking waves up to 10 feet and an increased risk of sneaker waves and strong rip currents to the Bay Area. Beachgoers are instructed to stay out of the water and off jetties, piers, rocks, and other infrastructure near the water, the weather service said. headlines.title: Teen arrested after reported shooting in downtown San Jose
headlines.description: A 17-year-old was arrested early Monday after police responded to a report of a shooting in downtown San Jose. Officers were called at about 12:16 a.m. to the 300 block of South First Street. When they arrived, they located a male who they attempted to detain. According to police, the suspect fled but was taken into custody after a short foot pursuit. Officers recovered a firearm. Police said no shooting victims were found. The 17-year-old was booked into Juvenile Hall. The investigation remains ongoing.

headlines.title: At-risk 13-year-old boy last seen in San Jose
headlines.description: The California Highway Patrol is asking for the public’s help finding a missing 13-year-old boy who is considered at risk. Damien Padilla was last seen early Sunday morning near Story Road and Lyndale Avenue in San Jose. He was wearing red sweatpants, a light-colored shirt and black shoes. He is described as 5 feet 10 inches tall and weighs about 130 pounds. An endangered missing advisory was activated by CHP on Sunday for the counties of Santa Clara, Alameda, San Joaquin, Stanislaus and Sacramento. Anyone who sees Damien Padilla is asked to call 911 immediately.

headlines.title: Palo Alto police investigate robbery, possible hate crime at Baylands preserve
headlines.description: Palo Alto police are investigating a robbery and possible hate crime that happened last week at the Baylands Nature Preserve. Police said the victim was walking along the Marsh Front Trail on Thursday when a group of three men passed him before attacking him and stealing his wallet. According to police, the suspects also yelled racial epithets at the victim during the assault. The victim called police and was treated for injuries to his face. Anyone with information is asked to contact the Palo Alto Police Department.

headlines.title: Project Open Hand marks 30 million meals served in San Francisco
headlines.description: A San Francisco nonprofit is celebrating a major milestone after delivering its 30 millionth meal to someone in need. Project Open Hand marked the occasion Monday by delivering its 30 millionth meal to client Nicholas Galarza, with Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi making the special delivery. Galarza, who is living with HIV, became a client during the pandemic. He receives weekly deliveries of meals and groceries, which he said helped him recover after losing his job and facing homelessness. NBC Bay Area’s Kris Sanchez has more in the video above.

headlines.title: Oakland councilmember offers $500 reward for tip on suspected illegal dumping
headlines.description: Could some cold, hard cash help crack down on illegal dumping in Oakland? One city councilmember thinks so and paid $500 to help figure out who recently left a bunch of stuff in one neighborhood. It all started when photos were shared across neighborhood social media pages showing what appear to be several people illegally dumping large furniture and other items in the street at Courtland Avenue near Redding Street in Maxwell Park. The neighborhood social media pages said they filed a 311 complaint about this but asked community members for additional information. Councilmember Kevin Jenkins, who represents the area, said seeing those photos struck a nerve for him. “I was absolutely fed up,” he recalled, noting he saw many people in the comments who felt the same way. Jenkins then posted a video on social media, offering to pay $500 of his own money to the first person to identify the people in the photos “Hey Oakland, I need your help. I have a $500 reward. This lady seems to have accidentally left her stuff on Courtland and Redding [Street], and I need to find out who she is,” he said in the post. In an interview with NBC Bay Area on Sunday, Jenkins said of the post, “I didn’t want to be assumptive, and maybe the person would be willing to get their stuff back.” “But we have to highlight this issue in the city. We have to make people afraid that they will get caught,” he continued. Lots of people responded to Jenkins’ post. He said he paid the $500 reward to the first person who offered information that lined up with the people in the photos. Jenkins plans to share that information with the city. “This is not normal, people should not have to live amongst trash and filth. A lot of people just want basic quality of life things in Oakland,” he continued. Jenkins and other city leaders are trying different approaches to address illegal dumping, which has been a pervasive issue in “The Town.” On Saturday, the city revived its Bulky Block Party events, giving residents a free event where they can dispose of unwanted large household items. The city plans to host more of these events on October 24 of this year and January 23 and April 24 of next year. Earlier this year, the council approved more funding for illegal dumping cleanup and also voted to double fines for illegal dumping to up to $5,000. Jenkins hopes the public call-outs help, too. After this first try at offering a reward, he thinks he’ll offer up more rewards in the future.

headlines.title: Stanford becomes first school to organize a player-led College Football Players Association chapter
headlines.description: The College Football Players Association, an organization advocating for unionization and collective bargaining, announced Monday that Stanford has become the first team to organize a player-led chapter. CFBPA executive director Jason Stahl said the goal is for other Atlantic Coast Conference schools join Stanford in forming chapters. That would create momentum for unionization and the ability for players to bargain with conferences over working conditions. Stanford players elected offensive lineman Fisher Anderson and linebacker Ernest Cooper as their representatives. “Stanford has been a pioneer and innovator not just in football but as a school in general,” Cooper said “This first-ever current player-led chapter at Stanford is just another example of this innovation. We want to be leaders in college football and show other schools how they can create a chapter on their campus because we believe this is the future of college football.” Anderson said the CFBPA will play a role in giving players a voice in all aspects of governing college football. “Over the past five years, college football has been rocked back and forth by the waves,” he said. “When a CFBPA chapter becomes a reality on every college football team, it would put down an anchor where there isn’t one right now for the sport. The chapters can then become the building blocks for conference-wide collective bargaining agreements, which would bring sustainability, transparency and player protections to a sport in need of all three.” The NCAA and conferences have been working with federal legislators on a Senate bill that would grant the NCAA an antitrust exemption to be able to enforce rules such as a salary cap and transfer restrictions. Some athletic directors have suggested collective bargaining as an alternative if federal legislation is not passed, but a number of obstacles related to giving college athletes employee status would have to be cleared. ___ AP college football: https://apnews.com/hub/college-football
headlines.source: The Associated Press | The Associated Press

headlines.title: High COVID-19 levels in parts of the Bay Area
headlines.description: A possible summer surge of COVID-19 in the Bay Area has public health leaders asking people to take precautions. Wastewater data in Santa Clara County and San Francisco shows high concentrations of the virus. Medium levels are present on the Peninsula and in the North Bay. Current virus levels are way below what they were last summer during a statewide surge. NBC Bay Area’s Gia Vang spoke with UCSF infectious disease expert Dr. Peter Chin-Hong about the latest numbers. Watch their conversation in the video player above.

headlines.title: Video captures dramatic lifeguard rescue at Santa Cruz's Seabright Beach
headlines.description: A dramatic rescue at Seabright Beach in Santa Cruz was caught on video, showing a teenage lifeguard battling rough surf to save a young swimmer. The man who recorded the video said a boy, about 10 years old, was overwhelmed by wave after wave. A 16-year-old lifeguard rushed into the water, held onto the boy and tried to pull him back to shore while being battered by the surf. Other swimmers attempted to help before another lifeguard reached the pair. “The waves, I wouldn’t say they were tranquil, but they were what you’d expect, a normal cadence and intensity,” witness Scott Vander Dussen said. “And then that just changed in a heartbeat. It caught a lot of people off-guard. Unfortunately, this young man was overwhelmed and swept out in just a moment’s time. I’m glad it ended the way it did. I’m certain if the lifeguards weren’t there, he wouldn’t have gone home that night.” Vander Dussen said the boy was evaluated by paramedics before being released to his parents. While officials did not discuss the specific training of the lifeguard involved, Santa Cruz lifeguards are required to complete at least 56 hours of lifeguard training, 24 hours of medical certification training and more than 80 hours of marine safety lifeguard training. Dangerous surf conditions are expected to continue through Wednesday.

headlines.title: Mines Fire in Santa Clara County reaches 40% containment
headlines.description: Firefighters have contained 40 percent of the Mines Fire in Santa Clara County, Cal Fire said early Monday morning. The fire, which was first reported just after 2 p.m. on Sunday, burned 132 acres of land and vegetation before CalFire crews stopped its spread in the area of Mines and San Antonio Valley roads. near the juncture of Alameda and Santa Clara counties. The cause of the fire was not immediately confirmed, as of 6:40 a.m. Monday. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates. Bay City News contributed to this report
headlines.source: Victoria Meza and Bay City News

headlines.title: Northbound Highway 101 lanes reopen after Brisbane crash
headlines.description: Multiple lanes on northbound U.S. Highway 101 in Brisbane reopened on Monday morning after a crash, the California Highway Patrol said. The crash occurred on the freeway north of Sierra Point, where three northbound lanes were blocked, according to a CHP social media post at 6:20 a.m. CHP officials said lanes reopened at 7 a.m. The cause of the crash was not immediately known. Motorists traveling through the area were urged to consider alternate routes. Bay City News contributed to this report
